standard.title: Strategies to increase activity and reduce sedentary behaviour
standard.description: propose and explain strategies to increase physical activity and reduce sedentary behaviour levels in their lives
standard.prior_knowledge: At Years 3-4, students explored recommendations about physical activity and sedentary behaviours and discussed strategies to achieve the recommendations (AC9HP4M06). They know that guidelines exist and can discuss strategies at a general level but have not yet proposed and explained strategies grounded in their own specific life contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students propose and explain strategies to increase physical activity and reduce sedentary behaviour in their own lives, with reference to health benefits and social and mental wellbeing.

nodes.label: Understanding the activity-sedentary balance
nodes.description: Explain the relationship between physical activity levels, sedentary behaviour, and health and wellbeing — going beyond knowing guidelines to understanding why the balance matters and what counts as sedentary vs active.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the difference between physical activity and sedentary behaviour, and explain at least one specific health or wellbeing consequence of each.
success_criteria: Correctly distinguishes physical activity from sedentary behaviour (e.g. light movement does not automatically mean 'active')
Connects sedentary behaviour specifically to a health consequence — not just 'it's bad for you'
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who lack the activity/sedentary distinction will propose strategies that address activity in isolation (do more exercise) without addressing sedentary reduction — the descriptor requires both. Strategies that only increase activity without reducing sedentary time may not achieve the health outcomes students are proposing.

response_modes.reason: Case study or time-audit analysis: map a typical day and classify each block as active, sedentary, or light movement. This builds the conceptual distinction through their own lived experience rather than abstract definition.

nodes.label: Examining benefits across health dimensions
nodes.description: Investigate the benefits of physical activity specifically for social health and mental wellbeing — not only physical health — to build a multi-dimensional rationale for the strategies students will propose.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one benefit of physical activity for mental or social wellbeing (not physical health) and explain how this benefit might influence strategy choices.
success_criteria: Names a social or mental wellbeing benefit specifically (not a physical health benefit reworded)
Connects the benefit to strategy design — e.g. 'because it also helps with social connection, we could design activities that involve others'
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The social and mental benefits of activity span many activity types and contexts — community options, school-based options, home-based options, digital/active combinations — each offering different dimensions of the benefit.

response_modes.reason: Research local physical activity options and their social/mental dimensions — community sport, lunchtime activities, active transport, nature-based activity. Each offers different social and mental wellbeing mechanisms.

nodes.label: Proposing and explaining personalised strategies
nodes.description: Propose and explain strategies tailored to their own life context — not generic recommendations but strategies that account for their actual routines, interests and environments.
nodes.minimum_width: Propose at least two strategies for their own life — one to increase physical activity and one to reduce sedentary behaviour — and explain why each is realistic and likely to be effective for them specifically.
success_criteria: Strategies are specific to the student's life context, not generic ('go for a walk' alone is insufficient)
Includes at least one strategy addressing sedentary behaviour specifically (not just adding activity)
Explains why the strategy is realistic for them — acknowledges their actual constraints

response_modes.reason: Integrates the activity/sedentary distinction, multi-dimensional benefits, and personal context into proposed strategies. This is the full descriptor demand — propose and explain strategies in their own lives.
